source: ACIAR / University of New England / CARE, "IPM Field Guide for Soybean Pest Management in Cambodia," ACIAR project field guide, 2006
text:
The guide profiles the main soybean pests and beneficial (natural enemy) insects farmers will find while scouting, each with an identification photo and a short "what to look for" note keyed to specific plant parts and damage symptoms:

Pest identification entries include: green stink bug and related shield bugs (labeled ស្រីងបែតង in the source, feeding on pods, causing shrivelled/discolored seed); a coreid/leaf-footed bug group (feeding on pods and stems, three egg-laying generations noted per season in the source's own count — the source's Khmer label for this species was not clearly enough legible to transcribe with confidence and is omitted here per project convention); an assassin bug (labeled ស្រីងគ្នាត in the source, predatory, beneficial rather than a pest); soybean aphid; grasshoppers; cutworm/armyworm caterpillars; pod borer; and bollworm/Heliothis-type caterpillars (Khmer common names for these last four were visible in the source but too small/unclear to transcribe with full confidence and are omitted here rather than guessed).

Beneficial insects are given equal billing so farmers learn to avoid killing them: ladybird beetles (អណ្ដើកមាស), hoverflies/syrphid flies (រុយសំកាំង, larvae feed on aphids), predatory wasps, praying mantis (កណ្ដបបុកស្រូវ), and other parasitic wasps — the guide's explicit point is that indiscriminate spraying kills these natural enemies along with the target pest, undermining long-term pest control.
